cards.tip: WIN — When the customer worried about what Shay promised, you said 'I don't want you to feel misled...you've been through a lot'—that honest reframe flipped her from skepticism to signing up for the VIP program because you built trust by clarifying instead of overselling.

FIX — When they said they want their new home working right, reconnect and build urgency: 'With a 20-year-old system, replacement is probably your best option—let me inspect and I'll show you options so we can get you set up today' instead of just scheduling a report back.

FIX — When customer expressed timeline and budget limits ('whatever we can finagle through'), you validated but didn't build options—add: 'I'll show you critical safety fixes and upgrades separate, so you pick what fits this month.' That reconnection + options (Decision move) is what flips the diagnostic into a TGL.

WIN — Andrew correctly identified the renter/landlord structure and pivoted to involve the decision-maker (Priscilla) rather than trying to sell a non-decision-maker on options she couldn't approve, enabling proper stakeholder engagement.

WIN — Mario executed a model inspection call: clear scope and timeline, systematic discovery questions, professional report framework. This sets up the next phase (delivering findings + options) for potential upsell.

FIX — When customers mentioned previous contractors had ripped them off, that was the objection-handling moment—Ben said 'I'm so sorry about that' but should've asked 'What happened with those companies?' to reconnect and show why the free evaluation would be different.

FIX — At the decision point, when the customer said the AC inspection was 'almost redundant' because the system is just two months old, you said 'There's no harm' instead of asking 'What does good comfort look like for you?'—the check-in question that would have surfaced whether they needed a maintenance plan or a second zone, turning the inspection into a TGL.

FIX — When your customer said their 2008 unit needs Freon every couple years and told you 'I don't know' about the issue, that was the moment to say, 'Let me check it out—if replacement turns out cheaper than ongoing service, would you want an estimate?' That's how you turn a maintenance call into a TGL without the hard sell.

WIN — When Ed mentioned his home warranty would cover a red-tagged furnace, Bradley offered "let me call my boss and we can send our guy over here," then proposed replacing only the attic unit instead of both—converting Ed's cost hesitation into a concrete, manageable path that secured his commitment to schedule the follow-up.
